recipes.name: Oven-Fresh Seasoned Potato Wedges
ingredients_raw: 2 russet potatoes, scrubbed and cut into eighths

steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Place potatoes, Parmesan cheese, olive oil, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, and pepper into a resealable plastic bag. Seal the bag, then shake until potatoes are evenly coated with seasoning.
Spread potatoes on a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until potatoes are easily pierced with a fork, about 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Oven-Fresh Seasoned Potato Wedges
raw_recipe.description: Potato wedges baked in the oven, seasoned with Parmesan, garlic powder, and onion powder. They're easy to make for a tasty side and sure to be a hit!

video.description: Crisp and perfectly seasoned potato wedges! Parmesan cheese and other great seasonings go into coating and making these delicious! Serve with a sandwich for a tasty meal!

review.reviewBody: Great seasonings in this recipe. I rated 4 stars because I made some changes - we boiled the potato wedges for 7 minutes before seasoning them and putting them in the oven for about 15 minutes. This makes for a great texture. It's mashed potatoey goodness inside, with a crispy outside. You cannot ask for anything more...great texture and less bake time with the par-boil technique.

Pretty tasty. I used sea salt. I did cook them for a little longer, only because we like them a little crispier. I served these with my Zesty Ranch Dip. No leftovers. Next time, I'll double the recipe.

Loved the technique and the texture of the potatoes, so 3 stars. However, the garlic powder and onion powder ruins the taste for us. Those two ingredients appear in so many commercial products, which is why I believe people don't mind them, or actually develop a taste for them. I was raised a second-generation Italian, and we never even had ersatz ingredients like those in the house. When we wanted garlic or onion flavor, we used garlic or onions. As a consequence, I can't stomach the flavor of artificial stuff. Instead, rubbing the cut potatoes with a cut clove of garlic and a cut onion will give a far superior flavor. That said, it's brilliant to combine the oil, Parmesan, salt, pepper and any other spices you like in a bag and shaking the potatoes is a very neat, no-fuss way to dress them before roasting. We eliminated the garlic and onion powders, replacing them with finely chopped rosemary and basil from the garden. Boo-ya!!! Great flavor that will complement any roasted meat or poultry.

I doubled the recipe, because POTATO WEDGES. Here's what I did different, though. I buttered 4 potatoes, then cooked them for 10 minutes. I let them cool, then buttered them again. The only reason I did this was because I really like crispy skins to begin with, but then I kind of ruin that by mixing the dry ingredients with 1 cup of flour, dipping the sliced potatoes in an egg mixture (2 eggs, 1/4 cup water), then dredging them in the dry mix. Followed the recipe after that, and I'll be doing it like that until I die of potato poisoning, if there is such a thing.

These were delicious and easy to make. If serving as a side, figure 1 potato per person, like a baked potato. The only thing I'll do differently next time is flip them halfway through so both sides get crispy.

added more oil … use 3 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil plus 3 tablespoons of vegetable oil … additionally, I added two heaping tablespoons of rice flour instead of the Parmesan cheese and hand-tossed in a deep bowl ( shaking in a bag risks breaking the wedges) !!!
Used 3 medium potato's which I microwaved for about 3 minutes to give them a little head start (which I'm glad I did). Turned them halfway through the cook time and they came out great.

I made this, delicious! I improved my cooking experience by also shaking (4) chicken thighs in the coating and baking them along side the potatoes on parchment paper on a cooky sheet. Put the thighs in first as they need and extra 10-15 minutes, while you are prepping the potatoes. (Why waste the oven heat, eh?). A couple of ears of corn, steamed in husk in the microwave, (3-4 minutes) shucked as soon as they were touchable. MMMM mmm, what a great meal with little clean up.

Great recipe! Added seasoned salt and also a bit of paprika, to other spices listed. Also took advice of reviewers who suggested microwaving a bit first (I nuked for about 8 minutes, since my wedges were large), to cut down on time in oven. Family loves this recipe; I have made for them several times. Also, hate wasting plastic bags, so mixed in a large glass bowl.

My family are these all up so fast!!!! I added garlic salt and used fine parmesan cheese. Soooo good! We like our food a bit crispy so I let them stay in the oven for ten minutes longer and they were absolute perfection. Both my kids and my husband devoured them all!!!

I took the advice from a reviewer and also boiled my sliced wedges for 7 minutes exactly and then dried them up and then seasoned then exactly as instructed. Then I baked them for 20 minutes and then turned them over for an additional 10 minutes cooking time. Came out so delicious!
Will make again.
I love these. I wouldn't change a thing.
great recipe, I used air fryer, so reduce temp to 400, 15 min, flipped put back in for 12 min, perfect.
We added oregano & chopped jalapeños, yummm
Very good.I love potatoes so this one is great!

Pretty good. I took some advice in the comments where they said they boiled the wedges for 7 minutes before seasoning & baking them. It took about 30 or so minutes for my oven to get them crispy to my preference, but it's pretty old, so it may take less time for you. Overall, pretty good! I may try again while boiling for less time, so they retain even more crunch.
My husband and I love these as an alternative to potatoes chips when we grill hamburgers! So yummy!
You can modify the seasoning to your heart's desire!
Super easy recipe and better than store bought wedges. I put mine in a bowl to coat. Trying to not use so much plastic.
